title: T-2 Toxin Neurotoxicity: Molecular Mechanisms and Emerging Chemoprotective Strategies
content: Mycotoxins can contaminate food and food raw materials and threat to animal and human health. T-2 toxin is the most toxic secondary metabolite mainly produced by Fusarium species among trichothecenes. T-2 toxin exposure can induce multiple toxic effects, including hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, immunotoxicity, gastrointestinal toxicity, reproductive toxicity. Recent studies reported that T-2 toxin can cross the he blood-brain barrier and trigger neurotoxicity. In this review, we summarized the neurotoxic effects caused by T-2 toxin exposure and the underlying molecular mechanisms. Additionally, the effective neuroprotective agents and potential clinical applications are discussed. Current studies revealed that molecular mechanisms of T-2 toxin-induced neurotoxicity involve oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, neuroinflammation, autophagy, ferroptosis and cell apoptosis. Several signaling pathways, including NFE2L2, NRF-2, PGC-1, p53, BTG2, AKNA, MAPK, Akt, mTOR, HMGB1, HIF-1, CREB, and NF-κB, are involved. Additionally, it was reported that several antioxidants, small inhibitors and nature products, such as daucosterol, betulinic acid, AHN 1-055 hydrochloride, dimethyl fumarate and minocycline supplementations can partly ameliorate these harmful effects. This review provides valuable insights into the underlying for T-2 toxin-induced neurotoxicity and novel effective detoxification strategies.
